newsitem.title: JORDAN: Iraq says seeks to expand trade with Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says seeks to expand trade with Jordan.

text.p: Iraq's Minister of Trade Mohammed Mehdi Saleh on Sunday said President Saddam Hussein wanted to expand existing trade ties with Jordan, waving aside political differences with Amman.
Officials said Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti would meet Saleh on Monday in a further attempt to end the strains in relations since King Hussein turned against Saddam last year.

Saleh told the Chamber of Industry Jordanians had a competitive egde in a range of industries, including vegetable oils and drugs, under the U.N deal that allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil every six months to buy humanitarian needs.
He said Iraq would give Jordanians who kept dealing with Baghdad despite U.N. sanctions over its 1990 invasion of Kuwait "preference, provided their prices were comparable."
"Under directives from the president, Iraq is open towards Jordan and there is no obstacle to expanding ties, except the financial constraint," Saleh said.
Businessmen say the government is now working to ensure Jordan does not lose out to others courting Iraq. They say good ties would help them recoup losses under the trade sanctions.

Jordanian industrialists also are counting on strong business ties, which weathered the political strains, to sell more medicine, vegetable oil and detergents that have been exempt from the U.N. blockade.
"I expect trade to increase and our aim is that it returns to its former levels. Iraq will give us preference," Khaldoun Abu-Hassan, head of Amman Chamber of Industry, told Reuters.

Jordan's businessmen feel vindicated for resisting pressure to curb ties with Baghdad and look to Israel. While echoing wide disappointment with the benefits of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, they say Iraq is Jordan's natural market.
The pro-Iraq business lobby is seeking restoration of a $400 million trade protocol they say was cut by half this year under U.S. pressure.

Most of Jordan's industrial exports to Iraq go through the the protocol, under which Jordanian industrial goods are traded for Iraqi oil. Saleh said Iraq was favourable to expanding the protocol, under which Baghdad sets its priorities of imports.
Jordanian officials say a team led by the energy and finance ministers will go to Baghdad soon to discuss extra oil imports that may open the way for lifting the protocol ceiling.

"In our next meetings we will discuss all the issues including the possibility of raising or adding (to the protocol)," Jordan's acting Trade Minister Nasser al-Lawzi, who participated in the discussions, told Reuters.
Iraq supplies Jordan with 75,000 barrels per day of crude and oil products, a deal exempt from the U.N. oil embargo on Iraq.
